paper-hybrid-gan-privacy-preservation-20.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid privacy-preservation scheme for Industrial IoT data that combines a GAN-based synthetic data generator with differential privacy, replacing only the sensitive columns with GAN-synthesized values before adding calibrated noise. The authors run experiments on four SCADA-type IIoT datasets, comparing their hybrid method against pure CTGAN synthesis and pure differential privacy in terms of linear-regression accuracy retention and privacy metrics. CTGAN, explicitly instantiated via the 'CTGANSynthesizer library', is the core synthetic-data generator whose output (XG) is used both as an intermediate stage of the proposed pipeline and as one of the baseline comparison methods.

paper-small-decoding-yes-decisions-2023.summary: This paper proposes a GAN-based method to address the small-data problem in brain-computer interfaces, converting motor-imagery EEG signals into frequency-domain features via power spectral density and generating synthetic samples to augment training data for decoding yes/no decisions in locked-in patients. Real and synthetic data are compared for statistical/visual similarity and via random forest classification, showing predictive gains from augmentation. CTGAN is used directly as the generative model, trained on the extracted EEG feature tables to produce the synthetic data underlying the entire empirical evaluation.

paper-atlas-gan-differentially-private-2.summary: This paper proposes ATLAS, a GAN-based framework for differentially private multi-party data sharing in which each party holds a discriminator and a central curator holds the generator, with two added techniques (collaborative discriminator filtering and adaptive gradient perturbation) to improve shared-data utility under DP noise. Experiments on real-world horizontally-partitioned datasets show ATLAS outperforms prior DP data-sharing baselines. The CTGAN paper is cited only as the source of the machine learning efficacy evaluation metric used to assess synthetic data quality, following standard practice in prior data-sharing work.
paper-atlas-gan-differentially-private-2.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is also run as an experimental baseline elsewhere in the paper.

paper-early-malware-threat-detection-202.summary: This conference paper proposes using CT-GAN (CTGAN) to generate synthetic tabular data addressing limited data availability and class imbalance in malware detection, training on the KDD_cup99 dataset and evaluating classifiers such as Gaussian-NB, decision tree, and random forest on CTGAN-generated data. The authors report accuracies exceeding 93% and describe CTGAN's mode-specific normalization, conditional generator, and reversible data transformations as the mechanism enabling this. CTGAN, the SDV-family tabular GAN, is run as the sole generator underpinning the entire empirical pipeline of the paper.

paper-bert-activity-recognition-sequence.summary: This paper proposes a human activity recognition pipeline that extracts skeleton pose features from video and classifies activity sequences with a BERT-based transformer, training and evaluating on the UP-Fall public dataset with GAN-based data augmentation to balance classes. The actual tabular data augmentation is performed with TABGAN (Ashrapov 2020), a separate library, chosen for its ready availability. CTGAN and TGAN are named only in a background sentence listing prior tabular-data-generation methods before the authors opt for TABGAN instead, so neither SDV-family model is run in the work.

paper-dyane-dynamic-attributed-node-2023.summary: This paper proposes DYANE, a generative model for dynamic attributed networks that combines temporal motifs with node-role-based content embedding generation, evaluated against other dynamic graph generative baselines on real-world co-authorship networks. Among the baselines is CTWalk, a prior model that generates temporal edges via TagGen and generates node/edge attributes via CTGAN, whose authors' implementation the DYANE paper runs directly for comparison. CTGAN itself is not modified or run independently by the DYANE authors but arrives embedded inside the CTWalk baseline they evaluate against.

paper-human-loop-machine-learning-2023.summary: This paper presents a Human-in-the-Loop Machine Learning (HITL-ML) system for deciding whether chemotherapy is suitable for pancreatic cancer patients, combining a dense neural network classifier with expert feedback used to iteratively refine a synthetic-data generator. The generator augments a small TCGA-derived dataset and is refined via expert-supplied constraints on invalid column combinations (e.g., FixedCombinations, GreaterThan rules). CTGAN, described by the authors as part of the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) project, is run directly as the synthetic case generator, with its SDV-style constraint mechanism used extensively to enforce clinically valid combinations in the generated data.

paper-spectral-clustering-augmentation-p.summary: This paper proposes SCAPC-GAIN, a GAN-based imputation method for multivariate time-series (EEG) data that uses spectral-clustering-derived pseudo-labels and an auxiliary classifier with missingness augmentation to improve imputation accuracy over prior GAN imputation baselines. The TGAN paper (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) is cited only in a background discussion of missing-data mechanisms, with no use of the SDV-family software in the method or experiments.

Cannot confirm whether TGAN/CTGAN methodology is used anywhere else in the paper.

paper-synthetic-development-status-prosp.summary: This paper is a survey/position piece that reviews the state of the art in synthetic data generation methods (process-driven and data-driven, including Copula-based, Bayesian network, and deep generative approaches), summarizes performance evaluation indexes and application fields, and proposes preliminary ideas for military applications of synthetic data such as training data augmentation and simulation scenario generation. SDV is cited descriptively as a Copula-based relational database synthesis toolkit developed by Patki et al. in 2016, described in prose rather than run in any experiment.

paper-synthetic-oil-chromatographic-samp.summary: This paper proposes a causal conditional GAN to generate synthetic oil chromatographic samples for electric power transformers, addressing scarce and imbalanced fault data by combining causal mechanisms with GAN conditioning, and evaluates diagnostic accuracy against a support-vector-machine classifier trained on synthetic versus real data. The generator itself is the authors' own Causal Conditional GAN, not an SDV model. The python package sdv.evaluation is run to score the generated data's overall quality, column shapes, and value/range fidelity, providing the quality-report metrics reported in the paper's results tables.

paper-effectiveness-augmentation-compres.summary: This work studies whether data augmentation can improve linear-regression prediction of compressive strength for calcined clay cements, aiming to support more sustainable, lower-CO2 cement formulations. In its background discussion of synthetic data generation methods, it briefly notes that copula-based models have proven effective for generating synthetic data, including for privacy protection, citing the original SDV paper without adopting or running it.

paper-autotuning-gaussian-copula-2023.summary: Tunes high-performance computing applications empirically, where each evaluation costs a full run and the search space is large. It is described as the first generative transfer-learning autotuning approach based on the Gaussian copula: prior tuning results are modelled and sampled to propose configurations for a new problem, so SDV's copula generates search points rather than data records.

paper-use-generative-adversarial-network.summary: This paper investigates whether synthetic survey data can substitute for real data in educational technology research, using a TPACK-based teacher self-perception survey as its dataset. The authors generate twenty-nine synthetic samples with four generative models -- TVAE, CTGAN, GaussianCopula and CopulaGAN, explicitly implemented per Patki, Wedge & Veeramachaneni (2016) -- and compare their fidelity and cluster-analysis outcomes against the real data. SDV's synthesizer suite (TVAE, CTGAN, GaussianCopula, CopulaGAN) is run directly as the set of generators whose outputs are evaluated and compared.

paper-artificial-intelligence-predict-or.summary: This paper applies an AI model to survey data from 44 respondents in Australian public and private organizations to predict future organizational agility, identifying practices and characteristics that support agility. To augment the limited survey data, the authors used the SDV Python package's Gaussian Copula model to generate 200 additional synthetic data points, and evaluated the fit of that synthetic data against the real dataset using SDV's KSTest metric. SDV's GaussianCopula synthesizer and its quality-evaluation metric are run directly as the mechanism for producing and validating the study's synthetic training data.

paper-active-learning-human-loop-2022.summary: This paper studies active learning strategies for human-in-the-loop customs fraud inspection, showing that a hybrid strategy combining likely-fraudulent and uncertain item selection outperforms exploitation-only approaches on real multiyear customs data from three countries. To enable reproducible experiments, the authors also release a synthetic import declaration dataset. CTGAN is used to generate this synthetic dataset of 100,000 artificial import records sharing data fields with the real customs data.

paper-commute-communication-efficient-tr.summary: COMMUTE proposes a communication-efficient transfer learning framework for multi-site risk prediction that shares only aggregated summary statistics rather than raw patient data across sites, reducing communication and preserving privacy. The authors contrast their approach with prior methods that protect privacy by generating and sharing synthetic data mimicking the original distribution, citing SDV among such methods. SDV is only cited as an example of a synthetic-data-based privacy approach, not run or adopted in the work.
paper-commute-communication-efficient-tr.needs: Full text not obtained; only the abstract-context citing sentence available, so depth of engagement with SDV beyond this contrastive mention cannot be confirmed.

paper-ctgan-imbalanced-ids-2022.summary: Treats intrusion detection as a class-imbalance problem first and a classification problem second, oversampling the attack classes of standard IDS benchmarks before fitting SVM, decision tree and neural classifiers, and separately scoring the quality of the generated records rather than only the downstream detection rate. CTGAN is the paper's method rather than one of its comparisons: it is run as the oversampler for every configuration, and the stated contributions are applying CTGAN to intrusion-detection imbalance and evaluating the data it generates.

paper-oog-optuna-optimized-gan-2022.summary: This paper proposes OOG, a pipeline that uses Optuna to hyper-tune GAN-based oversampling methods for generating synthetic malware samples to correct class imbalance, then classifies the augmented data with a weighted ensemble of boosting classifiers (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Extra Trees, Gradient Boosting), reporting 98.06% accuracy and comparing against SMOTE. The authors explicitly state that CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN models were used to create the malware data, with hyperparameters such as epochs, generator/discriminator dimensions and embedding dimensions tuned via Optuna. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE and CopulaGAN synthesizers are run directly as the generators producing the synthetic minority-class malware samples underpinning the whole empirical study.
paper-oog-optuna-optimized-gan-2022.needs: Evidence does not confirm which specific library implementation (sdv-dev package vs another source) was used, though CopulaGAN's presence strongly implies the SDV package.

paper-moisture-content-diagnosis-method-.summary: This paper presents a wireless acoustic sensor network (WASN)-based system for nondestructively diagnosing the moisture content of live tree trunks, using acoustic emission features augmented by a custom Conditional Tabular Wasserstein GAN-Gradient Penalty-L (CTWGAN-GP-L) model to expand a small offline dataset before classification via a grid-search-optimized LightGBM model. In its related-work discussion the authors cite the Tabular GAN (TGAN) paper, noting its data quality was limited by lacking conditional guidance, and describe how CTGAN's mode-specific normalization addressed non-Gaussian, multi-modal distributions -- ideas incorporated conceptually into their own CTWGAN-GP-L architecture rather than run via the SDV library itself.

paper-vine-copula-quantile-regression-20.summary: This remote-sensing paper develops a D-vine copula quantile regression method to retrieve soil moisture from dual-polarimetric SAR Sentinel-1 backscatter over vegetated terrain, modeling the joint dependence between radar observables and soil moisture via vine copulas. The work is a geoscience/statistics application paper rather than a synthetic-data paper. It cites the SDV-family vine-copula paper as a methodological reference for the vine copula construction used in its regression framework.

paper-multi-class-classification-detecti.summary: This conference paper builds a multi-class classifier for IoT botnet attacks using the IoT-23 and MedBIoT datasets, applying KNN imputation and ensemble methods (random forest achieving 99.88% accuracy) to categorize six botnet variants into three classes. The authors additionally generate synthetic samples to address data insufficiency for underrepresented attack variants (e.g., Torii) and to stress-test the robustness of their trained classifiers against newly generated data. CTGAN is run to produce these additional synthetic samples per attack variant, serving as an auxiliary data-augmentation and robustness-testing tool rather than the paper's core contribution.

paper-qualit-tsmanagement-und-vorausscha.summary: A German-language engineering paper proposing a methodology for generating synthetic datasets by combining technological expert knowledge with mathematical modeling, aimed at supporting quality management and predictive maintenance for small and medium manufacturing enterprises. It is illustrated through a component produced via internal high-pressure forming (IHU). The paper cites the original SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) DSAA 2016 paper as part of the synthetic-data literature, without describing any use of the SDV software itself.

paper-synthetic-tabular-generation-obliv.summary: This paper proposes an Oblivious Variational Autoencoder (OVAE) for generating synthetic tabular data, aimed at easing the scarcity of personal (e.g., health) tabular datasets available for open research while protecting privacy. It benchmarks OVAE against deep generative baselines including medGAN, VEEGAN, tableGAN, CTGAN and TVAE, and adopts CTGAN's mode-specific normalization technique to preprocess multi-modal continuous variables. CTGAN and TVAE, from the SDV family, are run as comparison baselines and their mode-specific normalization concept is incorporated into the authors' own preprocessing pipeline.

paper-analyzing-medical-research-results.summary: This paper validates statistical results derived from synthetic electronic medical record data (generated by the MDClone system) against results from real data across five observational clinical studies, finding strong concordance especially with larger sample sizes. It is a methodological validation study in medical informatics, not a synthetic-data-generation method paper itself. The Synthetic Data Vault (Patki et al. 2016) is cited only in the introduction and discussion as prior background literature on synthetic health data validation, with no SDV code or component run.

paper-implementation-analysis-clustering.summary: This paper proposes Q-Means, a novel data clustering algorithm designed to avoid the initial-value-selection sensitivity of K-Means, Fuzzy C-Means, and agglomerative clustering, and evaluates it on a self-collected software architectural styles dataset against RapidMiner and MATLAB benchmarks. The SDV paper is listed only in the reference list and is never discussed or used in the body of the text.

paper-tabcascade-flow-matching-2026.summary: Targets features that mix a discrete state with an otherwise continuous distribution, such as inflated zeros or missing codes, by generating a coarse categorical sketch of the row first and then conditioning a high-resolution flow-matching model on it through a guided probability path and data-dependent coupling, with a proof that the cascade tightens the transport-cost bound. SDV supplies both sides of the evaluation: CTGAN version 0.11.0 from the sdv-dev repository and TVAE are run as baselines, and the Shape and Trend scores that carry the fidelity results come from SDMetrics version 0.22.0.

preprint-enhancing-tabular-anomaly-detec.summary: This paper proposes PLAG, a pseudo-label-guided anomaly generation method for tabular anomaly detection that decouples anomaly quantification into feature-level abnormalities and uses a two-stage filtering strategy to produce high-fidelity synthetic anomalies, outperforming eight baselines. In its related-work discussion of generative approaches to tabular data, it cites CTGAN as an example of GAN-based architectures that suffer from unstable training and mode collapse, without running or comparing against it experimentally.

preprint-evaluating-machine-learning-mod.summary: This preprint systematically evaluates 15 machine learning models, including the TabPFN foundation model, for predicting post-wildfire debris flows from basin-scale rainfall, burn-severity, and terrain features across the western United States, using SHAP for feature importance and TabPFN-generated synthetic data to address class imbalance and limited training data. The actual synthetic augmentation used is TabPFN, not any SDV-family tool. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list, with no engagement or use of it found anywhere in the body text.

preprint-extreme-particle-acceleration-r.summary: This astrophysics paper compiles and analyses catalogues of black-hole X-ray binaries, correlating their >100 TeV gamma-ray luminosity with radio, X-ray, and orbital properties to identify what distinguishes gamma-ray-loud systems, and tests spatial association with unassociated LHAASO/HGPS gamma-ray sources. To build a synthetic population matching the distribution of their real X-ray binary sample for this spatial comparison, the authors use a Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN, Xu et al. 2019), a component of the SDV family, run directly as the generator of the synthetic comparison sample.
preprint-extreme-particle-acceleration-r.needs: Not fully certain whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or an independent implementation was used, though the citation and description match the SDV CTGAN paper closely.

preprint-self-reinforcing-controllable-s.summary: This preprint proposes RDDG, an in-context learning framework that uses LLMs guided by progressive chain-of-thought steps and a self-reinforcing feedback mechanism to synthesize relational/tabular data for improving downstream imbalanced classification. RDDG performs core set selection, extracts attribute relationships and constraints via LLM prompting, and iteratively refines generated batches using statistical and correlation-based quality feedback. CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) is cited only as one of several GAN-based tabular data generation methods in the related-work discussion, not run or compared against experimentally.

paper-tabular-diffusion-memorization-202.summary: Traces memorization in tabular generative models back to individual training records, scoring each by how strongly and how early it is memorized over training epochs, and uses that score to drop the highest-contributing rows before training, combining the filter with a cut-and-mix augmentation into DynamicCutMix, which lowers memorization ratios without measurable cost to fidelity or downstream utility. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the three generators the method is trained on and measured against, and they carry the paper's transferability claim, since labels derived from the diffusion model are applied to them to show the memorization signal generalises across model families.

paper-cents-2025.summary: Generates high-fidelity synthetic household electricity consumption traces, including rare and unobserved scenarios, for power-grid planning and simulation.

paper-scrnaseq-generative-2025.summary: Evaluates generative models on single-cell RNA sequencing, where rare cell types are exactly the ones an analysis wants to characterise and exactly the ones with fewest observations. Gaussian Copula is among the generators producing synthetic cells for the underrepresented types, an application of SDV to genomics rather than tabular records.

preprint-explainable-fair-anti-money-202.summary: This preprint proposes an end-to-end pipeline for explainable and fair anti-money-laundering detection, combining synthetic data generation, imbalance-aware classifiers (Random Forest, MLP) with F2-optimized thresholds, and SHAP-based explainability and fairness auditing. The authors construct a 10,000-record synthetic AML dataset with a binary target and extreme class imbalance to evaluate the pipeline under conditions mimicking production AML systems. SDV's Gaussian Copula model is run directly to generate the entire synthetic training dataset that the paper's empirical results rest on.

preprint-multistart-large-neighborhood-s.summary: This preprint develops a Multistart Large Neighborhood Search heuristic combined with a tensor-train optimizer for large-scale LNG transportation and trading problems spanning multi-year planning horizons, handling flexible contracts, fuel consumption, and tank sloshing constraints. The method is evaluated against a linear-programming baseline on historic and artificially generated data, showing substantial profit improvements. Because production instance data could not be disclosed for privacy reasons, the authors generated three artificial test instances using the SDV Python package to mimic the statistical patterns of the real data.

preprint-multi-faceted-evaluation-framew.summary: This paper introduces SynEval, an open-source evaluation framework for assessing the fidelity, utility, and privacy of synthetic tabular data (specifically LLM-generated product reviews), tested on outputs from ChatGPT, Claude, and Llama. It combines statistical similarity metrics, downstream ML utility tests, and privacy attacks (e.g., membership inference) into a unified toolkit. SDV's foundational paper is cited only as the source of the Total Variation Distance metric used for comparing discrete columns, and CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of GAN-based tabular data generation, with no SDV code run.
preprint-multi-faceted-evaluation-framew.needs: None; full-text search confirms no SDV-family code or tool is run, only bibliographic citations.

preprint-cggm-conditional-graph-generati.summary: This paper proposes CGGM, a GAN-based conditional graph generation model that integrates network topology with multi-dimensional node features to generate balanced synthetic traffic graph snapshots for anomaly detection in IoT networks, using an adaptive sparsity adjacency generator, a multi-head self-attention feature encoder, and a distribution-distance latent constraint. It is evaluated against graph-based baselines (GraphRNN, GraphSGAN) and tabular data generation baselines on UNSW-NB15 and CICIDS-2017 datasets. CTGAN is run as one of two tabular-data-generation baselines, compared on classification performance, T-SNE visualization, and Wasserstein/MMD/KSTest distribution-discrepancy metrics against the proposed CGGM model.

preprint-enhancing-automl-performance-im.summary: This preprint proposes a self-balancing pipeline that integrates traditional and generative oversampling/undersampling techniques with hyperparameter optimization to improve AutoML classification performance on imbalanced tabular datasets. Through a grid search over multiple datasets, samplers, and thresholds, the authors show sampling method choice can improve weighted F1 score by up to almost six percentage points over baseline. SDV's synthesizers (CopulaGAN, CTGAN, Gaussian Copula, TVAE, and FastML) are run directly via the SDV library as several of the oversampling methods evaluated within the pipeline's grid search.

preprint-generating-synthetic-locally-es.summary: This paper proposes the Local Resampler (LR), a k-nearest-neighbor-based synthetic data generator designed to control disclosure risk from outliers that are not detectable in marginal distributions, and evaluates it on simulated and real datasets against established synthetic-data tools. The SDV package is described as including copula-based and deep-learning methods and is run as one of the comparison benchmarks (alongside synthpop and FAST ML) against the author's proposed LR method. SDV's copula-based synthesis approach is treated as an evaluation baseline, run and compared against, not extended or modified.
preprint-generating-synthetic-locally-es.needs: Evidence does not specify which exact SDV synthesizer(s) (GaussianCopula, CTGAN, TVAE) were actually run in the benchmark; only 'copula and deep learning' methods are mentioned generically.

preprint-improve-fidelity-utility-synthe.summary: This preprint studies how to improve the fidelity and machine-learning utility of synthetic multi-sequence credit card transaction data generated by the CPAR model, proposing five data-centric pre-processing schemas that incrementally improve both fidelity metrics and downstream fraud-detection performance. The authors describe CPAR (Conditional Probabilistic Auto-Regressive Model) in detail and run it as the sole generative model in all their experiments, evaluating its output on marginal distributions, time dependencies, and classifier metrics. The Conditional Probabilistic Auto-Regressive model, provided through the open-source Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library, is run directly as the generator underpinning the entire empirical study.

preprint-undermining-image-text-classifi.summary: This preprint proposes adversarial attack strategies against machine learning classifiers, combining GANs and SMOTE to generate data that fools text classification models trained on financial fraud data, and applying FGSM perturbations guided by GradCAM to attack a CNN-based face recognition system. The text-classifier attack pipeline uses CTGAN, run with its default hyperparameters (epochs, batch size, generator/discriminator dimensions, noise embedding dimension), to generate additional adversarial data points from cases the classifiers had misclassified. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is one of the two generative techniques (alongside SMOTE) that directly produce the adversarial data underlying the text-classification attack results.

preprint-linear-reconstruction-attribute.summary: This paper introduces a new attribute inference attack against synthetic data based on linear reconstruction of aggregate statistics, targeting all records rather than only outliers, and evaluates it against state-of-the-art SDG algorithms including probabilistic graphical models, GAN-based models, and differentially private mechanisms. The authors empirically test their attack and prior attacks on CTGAN alongside BayNet, RAP, IndHist and NonPrivate baselines, measuring accuracy against synthetic data size and privacy-utility tradeoffs. CTGAN is run as one of several evaluation-subject generators, its outputs subjected to the proposed inference attack and compared with the other synthesizers rather than being extended or reimplemented.

paper-association-rule-gan-hybrid-2023.summary: Combines range-based association rule sampling with a modified tabular GAN to handle imbalanced classification in automation settings. The modification to the generator makes this a derivative rather than a use, though the abstract does not state which parts were changed.

preprint-federated-learning-base-station.summary: This paper investigates federated learning for cellular traffic prediction, comparing five neural network architectures trained in a federated setting on non-identically distributed base station LTE data, and additionally explores a large-scale simulation with synthetic data to assess computational and communication costs. The paper cites the DeepEcho PAR paper on sequential models in the Synthetic Data Vault only in its reference list, with no engagement in the body text.

preprint-predictive-modeling-clinical-tr.summary: This preprint proposes a digital-twin approach to simulating clinical trials, building patient models from gene expression, drug, and cell-line similarity data drawn from TCGA and DrugBank to predict survival probability under drug combinations. Synthetic patient records are generated to construct observation and control groups for simulated trials, allowing trial parameters to be optimized before real-world testing. The authors explicitly use the SDV library's CTGAN module to generate this synthetic patient cohort data.

preprint-risc-generating-realistic-synth.summary: This paper introduces RISC, an open-source Python package and pipeline for generating realistic synthetic bilingual (French/English) automobile insurance contracts, and RISCBAC, a dataset of 10,000 unannotated synthetic contracts derived from Quebec's mandatory car insurance form, intended to support NLP research on long legal documents. To synthesize the numerical protection/coverage data within contracts, the authors trained TVAE and CTGAN models and compared their KS-test and unique-combination statistics to select the best generator. SDV's TVAE and CTGAN implementations are run directly as the generators for the tabular protection data, compared against each other, with TVAE selected as the final model.

paper-utility-theory-synthetic-2023.summary: Builds a theory of when synthetic data is useful, separating the utility of a downstream model trained on synthetic rows into a term for how well the generator approximates the real distribution and a term for the downstream task itself, and shows that closing the distributional gap is sufficient without requiring the generator to be consistent everywhere. The empirical program rests entirely on SDV: CopulaGAN, GaussianCopula, CTGAN and TVAE are the four generators the theory is instantiated on, each trained at varying sample sizes and scored through a downstream linear SVM.

preprint-generative-modeling-complex-202.summary: This preprint introduces a generic framework for synthesizing complex, nested/hierarchical data (structs and lists) using composite generative models called codecs, implemented with causal transformers, and shows it outperforms prior tabular and relational generators on standard benchmarks including a NIST hierarchical census dataset and Netflix Prize data. The authors evaluate against several Synthetic Data Vault models -- GaussianCopula and TVAE (retrained from the SDV GitHub repository), plus CTGAN, CopulaGAN, and HMA1 -- as baselines their model is compared against and generally outperforms. SDV's GaussianCopula, TVAE, CTGAN, CopulaGAN and the relational HMA1 algorithm are run as comparison baselines against the authors' proposed transformer-based codec model.

The work is aimed at improving trust in synthetic data for health data sharing. It cites the original SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) DSAA 2016 paper, though the abstract does not specify whether SDV itself is among the four generators actually run in the comparison.
